- What Is Mid-Market Sales?


Mid-market sales is the practice of selling to medium-sized businesses. While definitions vary, the[National Center for the Middle Market (NCMM)](https://www.middlemarketcenter.org/middle-market-101/) defines US middle-market companies as those with $10 million to $1 billion in annual revenue.


These organizations have larger budgets than small-to-medium sized businesses (SMBs), but they’re leaner than enterprises. That translates to greater agility and faster time to market, along with the potential for larger contracts.


That can be an advantage for business-to-business (B2B) sales professionals. Not only are you working with fewer decision-makers, but some mid-market buyers may have more developed purchasing requirements than smaller businesses.


Here’s a closer look at what’s considered mid-market in sales, and how selling into this segment plays out differently from SMB or enterprise deals.


## **Key Points**


- Mid-market sales targets medium-sized businesses that sit between SMBs and enterprises.
- While definitions vary, the National Center for the Middle Market (NCMM) defines US middle-market companies as those with $10 million to $1 billion in annual revenue.
- Medium-sized businesses make up more than 40% of the global workforce, according to[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/transformation/our-insights/unleashing-the-power-of-midcap-companies) . The global consulting firm defines them as organizations with $200 million to $2 billion in revenue—a different threshold than the NCMM uses.
- Mid-market companies usually have a more defined buying process than SMBs, with multiple decision-makers. But because they’re leaner than enterprises, deals often move more quickly through the sales cycle.
- Despite economic uncertainty,[82% of mid-market businesses](https://www.cpapracticeadvisor.com/2026/07/29/u-s-middle-market-sees-double-digit-growth-as-ai-fuels-shift-toward-productivity/187548/) report year-over-year (YoY) growth. And more than half (59%) expected to increase their workforce through mid-2027.


## **How Mid-Market Companies Are Defined**


Definitions of mid-market vary by source, but most center on the idea that they’re businesses too big to be SMBs and too lean to be enterprises. The NCMM sets its benchmark at $10 million to $1 billion in annual revenue, whereas global consulting firm[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/transformation/our-insights/unleashing-the-power-of-midcap-companies) defines them as organizations with $200 million to $2 billion in revenue.


Mid-market businesses can be either public or private. Some are family-owned or sole proprietorships. They exist in nearly every industry, especially service-oriented fields like:


- Healthcare
- Construction
- Manufacturing
- Financial services
- Retail
- Wholesale
- Education
- Business services


Regardless of definition or industry, mid-market companies are[essential to the US economy](https://www.uschamber.com/economy/rsm-u-s-chamber-middle-market-business-index) , accounting for one-third of total jobs and 40% of the gross domestic product (GDP) in the US.


## **How Mid-Market Sales Differs from SMB and Enterprise Sales**


The mid-market operates differently from SMBs or enterprises. They typically have faster sales cycles than enterprises, but they may involve more decision-makers than SMB sales do.


Here’s how deal size, decision-makers, and sales cycle length compare across the tiers.


### **Mid-Market vs. SMB Sales**


SMBs account for roughly[99.9% of all US companies](https://advocacy.sba.gov/2026/02/03/frequently-asked-questions-about-small-business-2026/) and employ over 62 million people.


Because they’re leaner, SMBs tend to move faster than mid-market companies. You might work with only 1 or 2 decision-makers, which can considerably shorten the sales process. An SMB sales cycle can take as little[as a couple of weeks](https://www.startups.com/lexicon/sales-cycle-length) , whereas a mid-market cycle might take a couple of months. Actual timelines depend on the company and the size of the deal, of course.


SMB budgets look a lot different. According to[Growth List](https://growthlist.co/enterprise-vs-smb-saas-strategy/) , the average SMB deal size is between $1,200 and $25,000, compared to about $25,000 to $50,000 for mid-market deals.


### **Mid-Market vs. Enterprise Sales**


Enterprises sit at the top of the ladder, and many are on the Fortune 500 list. To make[this list](https://fortunemedia.mediaroom.com/2026-06-03-Amazon-Claims-No-1-Spot-on-the-Fortune-500) in 2026, a company needs at least $7.5 billion in annual revenue. Fortune 500 companies make up two-thirds of the US GDP and employ 30.5 million people globally. That’s roughly 61,000 employees per enterprise.


Not every enterprise is a Fortune 500 company, but the typical annual revenue for businesses in this category might start in the 9-figure range. Budgets scale accordingly, with[enterprise deal sizes](https://www.arcade.software/post/enterprise-sales-cycle) commonly running between $50,000 and $500,000.


The trade-off is that enterprise sales cycles might stretch out across[6 to 18 months](https://www.apollo.io/insights/what-is-enterprise-sales) . Note that timing varies based on the offering, price, customer, approval processes, and other factors that can impact deal complexity. That’s because enterprises often have multi-department approval chains.


**Average deal size** **Average sales cycle length** **Buying group**


**SMB** ~$1,200–$25,000 14+ days Usually smaller


**Mid-market** ~$25,001–$49,999 Several months Multiple stakeholders


**Enterprise** ~$50,000–$500,000 6–18 months Often large and cross-functional


## **What Does a Mid-Market Sales Strategy Look Like?**


Now that you know what mid-market sales means in theory, what does a sales strategy look like in practice? While every business (and customer) is different, here’s the general process:


- **Identify your exact customer.** Break the mid-market into smaller segments so you can tailor your solution and messaging to the buyer you’re trying to reach. You build segments around size, geography, or vertical.
- **Understand their constraints.** Mid-market firms are at different growth stages, so dig into the problems they’re facing and any budget or timeline pressures. Then adjust your sales strategy accordingly.
- **Balance different types of selling.** Selling to the mid-market takes time, so try to balance consultative selling with faster-moving transactional sales. Consultative sales take longer, but can give you clarity into your customer’s motivations, typical sales cycle, and specific needs.
- **Use case studies or account-based approaches.** Existing case studies show what’s working and what isn’t. You can also use account mapping to get a clearer picture of the customer’s organization and decision drivers. This also helps identify the right stakeholders or other ideal customers.


Mid-market firms won’t have enterprise-level budgets or require quite as much customization. But they still benefit from clear segmentation, tailored solutions, flexibility, and ongoing support.


## **Building a Career in Mid-Market Sales**


Mid-market firms posted an average[7.3% YoY growth](https://www.middlemarketcenter.org/expert-perspectives/year-in-review-2025-wrapped-for-the-middle-market) in employment in 2025. That’s welcome news if you’re considering a career in this segment.


But is mid-market sales the best fit for you? Before taking the leap, here’s what the role looks like day-to-day versus SMB or enterprise:


- You’ll likely be selling to businesses with 100 to 1,000 or so employees. That means you might deal with several decision-makers to secure a sale. In many cases, this involves engaging with decision-makers in the C-suite, such as CTOs, CFOs, and more.
- Deals are bigger than what you’d see with SMBs but smaller than enterprise contracts. More is on the line, and commissions can follow suit.
- Sales cycles might last 1 to 3 months. That’s slower than SMB deals but significantly faster than most enterprise-level sales cycles.
- Quick deals might be rare, but the mid-market is a solid middle ground for consultative and transactional selling. Sales are also less complex than at the enterprise level.


Ultimately, the mid-market could be a good entry point into a sales career, especially if you’re interested in consultative selling, a needs-based approach that positions the seller as a trusted advisor.


## **Start Your Mid-Market Sales Career Today**


[Mid-market sales jobs](https://www.intuit.com/careers/teams/sales/mid-market/?cid=seo_blog_gen_us_sales-fy27_lg_v1_link_inti-tm) can be rewarding work. The median base salary for a mid-market account executive sits at about[$95,000 a year](https://www.repvue.com/salaries/mid-market-account-executive) , and experienced professionals could earn well above that.[According to SaaStr](https://www.saastr.com/sales-rep-annual-quotas-what-high-performers-are-actually-carrying/) , high-performing mid-market sales representatives in 2026 are carrying average annual quotas of approximately $1.35 million, highlighting the scale of the opportunities and performance expectations that come with the role.


As a mid-market B2B sales professional, you can work in nearly any industry. With bigger budgets and shorter cycles than enterprise sales, the mid-market is a strong place to build a lasting career, especially if you’re drawn to a mix of consultative and transactional selling.

## **FAQ** s


###


Mid-market firms are often privately held and generate between $50 million and $1 billion in annual revenue. Two examples are Clif Bar & Company ([$506.2 million](https://rocketreach.co/clif-bar-company-profile_b5c62060f42e0ca4) ) and CorMedix Therapeutics ([$311.7 million](https://cormedix.com/cormedix-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial-results-and-provides-business-update/) ).


###


SMB buyers often want fast, inexpensive solutions and results. Enterprise sales might involve much more customization. So, for mid-market sales strategies, a combination of account mapping, case studies, and consultative sales tends to work well. It also helps keep your solutions flexible so you can continue to provide reliable support as the company scales.


###


If you want to break into a mid-market sales career, you could start in SMB sales and work your way up from there. As you build your career, focus on less transactional sales cycles and more consultative work. Mid-market sales cycles are often longer and more complex than SMBs, so the more experience you have here, the better.
